questions.q: What does a head's attention pattern represent?
options: The head's final output logits for the vocabulary
A `(seq_len, seq_len)` matrix showing how much each position attends to each other position
The gradient of the loss with respect to that head's weights
The number of parameters contained in that single head
questions.explain: The attention pattern is the weight matrix itself: row i, column j is how much position i attends to position j.

questions.q: What did Clark et al.'s "What Does BERT Look At?" find when analyzing BERT's 144 attention heads?
options: That every head behaves identically regardless of layer or position
That heads show consistent, specific patterns -- attending to delimiters, fixed offsets, or syntactic relationships like a verb's direct object -- with heads in the same layer behaving similarly
That attention patterns are entirely random and carry no structure
That BERT has no attention heads capable of tracking syntax
questions.explain: The paper found real structure: delimiter-attending heads, positional-offset heads, and heads that align with syntactic relationships like direct objects and coreference.

questions.q: Why is ablation necessary even after visualizing a head's attention pattern?
options: Ablation is not necessary; a clear attention pattern always proves causal importance
Because a head's pattern can look meaningful while the model still ignores that head's actual contribution to its output, so ablation tests whether it's causally load-bearing
Ablation is only used to speed up inference, not to test importance
Attention patterns cannot be computed without first ablating a head
questions.explain: A visually interesting pattern doesn't guarantee the head's output actually matters to the model's behavior; ablation tests that directly by removing the head and measuring the effect.

questions.q: In the lesson's ablation code, what does a large drop in logit difference from clean to ablated indicate?
options: That the ablated head was not important to the model's preference for the correct token
That the ablated head was causally important for the model's preference for the correct over the incorrect token
That the model's vocabulary size has changed
That the forward hook failed to execute
questions.explain: A large drop means removing that head substantially weakened the model's preference for the correct answer, indicating real causal importance.

questions.q: What is a "previous token head," as named in this lesson?
options: A head that attends from the current position to the immediately preceding position
A head that only ever attends to the first token in a sequence
A head that deletes the previous token from the residual stream
A head found exclusively in vision transformers
questions.explain: A previous token head attends from position t to position t-1, a recurring functional category used throughout mechanistic interpretability's circuit analysis.
